$comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH for the website's design tokens (blueprint Phase 2).
scripts/gen-tokens.cjs emits web/src/styles/tokens.css from this file.
scripts/verify-tokens.cjs audits every declared colour pair for WCAG
contrast and fails CI on a violation. Edit this file, not the CSS.
WHY JSON RATHER THAN HAND-WRITTEN CSS
A palette is only trustworthy if its contrast is checked, and checking it
means machine-reading the values. Keeping them here makes the audit exact
instead of a regex over a stylesheet, and keeps one definition rather than
one per theme block.
The palette is derived, not invented: the dark theme is src/style.css (the
in-game HUD) verbatim where it can be, and the world colours come from
docs/ART_BIBLE.md. The site and the game should read as one object.

meta.concept: cartographer's table — parchment ground, survey ink, the game's own glass HUD on top
meta.lightIs: parchment: the surveyed map, seen by day
meta.darkIs: the game's dusk-blue HUD over a warm ember ground

$comment: Google Fonts only. Blueprint §8.1 permits fonts.googleapis.com and
fonts.gstatic.com and no other external host, so any face not on Google
Fonts has to be self-hosted before it can be used.
Every stack ends in a real system fallback: the page must be legible
before, and if, the webfont arrives.

display.stack: 'Fraunces Variable', 'Fraunces', 'Iowan Old Style', 'Palatino Linotype', Palatino, Georgia, serif
display.why: A variable serif with optical-size and soft/wonk axes — it has genuine character at display sizes instead of the neutral geometric sans every indie game page uses. Reads as almanac/survey, which is the concept. Optical sizing means the same family stays sane at small sizes.

body.stack: 'Inter Variable', 'Inter', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif
body.why: Humanist sans designed for screens, variable, excellent at the 16-18px body sizes the devlog needs. Deliberately quiet so the display face carries the personality.

mono.stack: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace
mono.why: Build IDs, version stamps, wiki data tables and code blocks. Unambiguous zero and clear 1/l/I, which matters when someone is comparing two build IDs by eye.

radius.$comment: lg is 16px — the game HUD's --radius, verbatim, so panels match.

$comment: Fluid, ~1.25 at mobile widening to ~1.333 at desktop (blueprint §3.4).
clamp() rather than breakpoints so nothing jumps size mid-resize, which
is a CLS source as well as an ugly one.

measure.$comment: Body copy caps at 68ch (blueprint §3.4); narrow is for captions and asides.

$comment: Blueprint §6.2 and §6.1.3, and M12a. Two bands, deliberately: the
world moves slowly and the interface answers fast — which mirrors
the game, a 600ms tick engine under a responsive HUD.
Every duration is now DERIVED from --tick rather than being a round
number that happened to sit near a tick fraction. The rendered
values barely move (only dur-base, 320ms -> 300ms), but the site
now moves at the engine's heartbeat by construction, and retuning
the whole motion system is one number. The trust row's pulsing dot
already runs at this interval; now everything else does too.
--tick is NOT collapsed under prefers-reduced-motion. It is a fact
about the game, not a duration; the dur-* tokens are overridden
directly instead, so nothing can reintroduce motion by reading it.

light.$comment: Parchment. The surveyed map by day.

dark.$comment: The game's HUD, verbatim where possible, over a warm ember ground.

$comment: WCAG 2.2 AA is a gate, not a preference (blueprint §9.2).
min 4.5 = normal body text.
min 3.0 = large text (>=24px, or >=18.66px bold) and non-text UI such as
borders, focus rings and icon strokes.
Every rule below is checked in BOTH themes unless it names one.

forbidden.why: Gold on parchment. Blueprint §3.3 bans it as body text — it is a border, rule and glyph colour only. Asserted to FAIL so the ban stays true: if a palette edit makes this pass, the ban is stale and should be reconsidered deliberately rather than silently.
The HUD blue is a fill/mark on parchment, not text. district-frostwatch is the text-safe variant.
Route-anchor orange is a map fill. district-cinder is the text-safe variant.
